source.title: Algebraic Representability as the Limiting Regime of Grokking: An Exactly Solvable Model with Holomorphic Activations
source.authors: Chon-Fai Kam; Xavier F. Cadet; M. Bessafi; Frédéric Cadet

record.tranche_reason: The study measures train–test timing and grokking outcomes on modular tasks using architectures and encodings different from the original studies, and tests how representability and bottleneck capacity affect those outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own training outcomes for holomorphic networks, ReLU networks, bottlenecked networks, and learned-embedding variants. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows. The paper does not measure a shrinking-training-set sweep, Fourier-circuit formation, or initialization-scale and weight-norm effects.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own train/test timing on modular-arithmetic tasks for several architectures. ReLU baselines and a bottleneck sweep show delayed generalisation. Holomorphic and learned-embedding networks fit train and test together, with no delay. This bears on whether V1's delayed jump holds. The training fraction is fixed at 40%, so the dataset-size part of V1 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also say the bottleneck sweep shows the grokking gap grows continuously as capacity shrinks toward the memorisation threshold. They frame their holomorphic result as the limiting FAIL regime of a capacity spectrum, adjacent to rather than competing with existing capacity accounts.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a two-layer complex-valued monomial network with roots-of-unity inputs, and also ReLU and bottlenecked-ReLU comparisons; these differ from the original grokking and mechanistic-interpretability setups. The training fraction is fixed rather than swept.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with representability and bottleneck dimension: d ≤ 2 fails, d = 4 or 8 memorises without generalising within the budget, and d ≥ 16 groks with a decreasing reported gap. Under learned embeddings the roots-of-unity versus random-phase initializations produce different aggregate INST counts and reported grokking outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: In the bottleneck sweep, the grokking gap shrinks monotonically as capacity grows: 15000 steps at d=16 down to 5250 at d=128. Below d=16 the network memorises without generalising, and at d≤2 it fails to fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The grokking delay is governed by model capacity: it lengthens as capacity approaches the memorisation threshold and vanishes or becomes failure below it.

fits_no_version.finding: With learned embeddings, a pre-fit acquisition delay grows with activation degree: step to 90% solved rises from about 3800 at k=2 to about 7900 at k=6. It is followed by a simultaneous train–test fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A representation-acquisition delay can occur without any memorisation-then-generalisation gap.

record.problems: The paper studies a specific two-layer architecture and modular tasks. It fixes the training fraction rather than testing the claimed relation between training-set size and optimization time. The bottleneck experiment has three seeds per dimension; uncertainty intervals are not reported. The paper's numerical results do not test the V2–V7 mechanisms.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcome directly testing V2–V7 was omitted. The learned-embedding step-to-90%-solved values (Table 4) measure acquisition time before train–test fit, not a post-overfitting generalisation delay, so they are not recorded as V1 rows.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size: the training fraction is fixed at 40%.
All parts; no circuit formation or progress measures are reported.
All parts; there is no non-algorithmic data and no initialisation-scale or weight-norm sweep.
All parts; weight decay is not varied and no critical dataset size or ungrokking is measured.

missing.what: Outcome distribution of the ReLU baseline over all 117 runs: INST / PART / GROK fractions (about 57%/36%/7% in the figure; category mapping unclear). Never FAIL.
Distribution of ReLU generalisation gaps among successful runs, ranging from 0 to 7500 steps.

record.verdict_notes: The ReLU baseline uses weight decay 1.0 and 8000 steps, described as the grokking-literature recipe, so R4 is close to T1. Rows where training never fits (R1, R6, R7) cannot speak to V1, since V1 presupposes training saturation. The study is not an original source. Preprint; there are three seeds per setting and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not vary training-set size, so it does not test whether smaller training sets require more optimization. Its main holomorphic experiments use 40% of the 9409 input pairs.
No circuit formation, memorizing-component removal, or continuous mechanistic progress measure is measured.
The tasks are modular arithmetic, not non-algorithmic image, text, or molecule data. The paper does not sweep initialization scale or weight norm, or test a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is studied.
Weight decay is used in some training recipes but is not varied or tested as an efficiency mechanism. No critical dataset size or ungrokking threshold is measured.
The study does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
The study reports one optimization exception but does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifacts as explanations for grokking.

rows.subject: two-layer complex-valued holomorphic monomial network
rows.operation_detail: Train on the fixed roots-of-unity encoding using full-batch AdamW.

conditions.value: 510 runs predicted to FAIL; p = 97, k = 2, 3, 4, 5, 6

rows.measure: Training outcome; FAIL means training accuracy never exceeds 99%, described as staying at chance level (1/97 ≈ 1%).
rows.value: 510/510 predicted-FAIL runs observed FAIL; none generalised.
rows.note: These runs did not reach the overfitting condition in V1: the paper says non-representable tasks could not be fit, with no memorization or grokking.
rows.check: Training accuracy never leaves chance, so V1's precondition (training saturates) is never met. The absence of grokking here cannot show that V1's delay is absent; 'absent' overstates it.

rows.subject: two-layer complex-valued holomorphic monomial network
rows.operation_detail: Train on representable tasks with the fixed roots-of-unity encoding.
rows.value: 74 runs were INST; the paper reports no MEM or GROK outcomes.
rows.note: INST is defined as both train and test accuracy exceeding 99% with a gap under 200 steps. The paper describes these successes as almost instant and without a train–test gap.
rows.check: State is correct. Training saturates and test accuracy follows within 200 steps, so there is no delay.

rows.subject: two-layer complex-valued holomorphic monomial network
rows.operation_detail: Train the k = 6, a + 5b cell, then rerun with a longer budget and gradient clipping.
rows.value: The initial run was the single representable-cell exception; rerunning with 8000 steps and gradient clipping drove training loss to zero at all seeds.
rows.note: The paper calls the initial shortfall a transient optimization issue. It does not report a delayed train–test transition for this cell.
rows.check: This is a single optimisation shortfall later resolved by longer training. It reports no train–test timing and should not be linked to V1.

rows.subject: standard two-layer ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Train on the same modular tasks with one-hot inputs.

conditions.value: nonlinear-phase targets ab, a² + b, a + b², a² + b²

rows.measure: Train–test generalisation gap in steps; both accuracies exceed 99%.
rows.value: For these harder targets, test accuracy lagged training accuracy by 3700–7500 steps.
rows.note: The paper describes these as grokking outcomes on the same tasks that the holomorphic network could not represent.

rows.subject: standard two-layer ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Train on the same modular-task grid.
rows.measure: Qualitative time between memorization and generalization.
rows.value: The paper says these targets generalised more quickly, with the gap shrinking as the arithmetic structure became easier to exploit.
rows.note: No per-task gaps are given for this group.
rows.check: Qualitative only. Figure 2 places these runs in INST/PART categories with shorter gaps; no per-task values are given.

rows.subject: bottlenecked ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular addition with a linear bottleneck.
rows.value: FAIL; training accuracy stayed at chance.
rows.note: The paper groups d = 1 with d = 2 in the table; the text says d ≤ 2 cannot fit the training data.
rows.check: Training stays at chance, so V1's precondition is not met; 'absent' overstates it.

rows.subject: holomorphic monomial network with learned complex embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Jointly optimize embeddings, network weights, and output weights.
rows.value: 186 of 190 cells were INST; no MEM outcomes. The paper reports no clean GROK cells under random-phase initialization.
rows.note: The paper says training and test accuracy mostly cross together. The reported cell counts are aggregates, not per-seed rates.

rows.subject: holomorphic monomial network with learned complex embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Jointly optimize embeddings, network weights, and output weights.
rows.value: 177 of 190 cells were INST; no MEM outcomes; the paper reports six clean GROK cells and a handful of borderline cases.
rows.note: The study does not give exact counts for the borderline cases in this passage; it describes the successful cells as overwhelmingly INST.
rows.check: The value is right: 6 clean GROK cells plus borderline cases out of 190. The count of borderline cases is not given.

rows.subject: holomorphic monomial network with learned complex embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Track train and test loss at 10-step resolution for representative learned-embedding cells.
rows.measure: Train–test loss and first crossing of 99% accuracy.
rows.value: Train and test loss descend together; the curves first exceed 99% accuracy within one 10-step logging interval (gap ≤ 10 steps).
rows.note: These examples do not show a long post-overfitting delay.

relationships.condition: Standard one-hot ReLU MLP on nonlinear modular targets; bottlenecked ReLU with d ≥ 16 on modular addition
relationships.reason: Test accuracy lags training accuracy by 3700–7500 steps (R4), and by median gaps of 15000 to 5250 steps (R10–R13).
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy lagged training accuracy by 3,700–7,500 steps on nonlinear modular targets, with bottlenecked modular addition showing median gaps from 15,000 to 5,250 steps.

relationships.condition: Holomorphic monomial network, with fixed roots-of-unity or learned embeddings, on representable tasks
